chunks: Ismail ibn Qutayba said: I and Isa Shalaqan went to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and he initiated us by saying: How strange are those people who claim things against the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) that he never uttered at all! The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) addressed the people at Kufa and said:

Praise be to God, the Inspirer of His servants to praise Him, and who created them upon the recognition of His Lordship — the One who points to His existence through His creation, and through the temporal origination of His creation to His pre-eternity, and through their mutual resemblance to each other to the fact that there is no resemblance to Him. He testifies through His signs to His power. His Essence is precluded from attributes, His being seen is precluded from eyes, and comprehending Him is precluded from imaginations.

There is no time-limit to His being and no end-point to His permanence; the senses cannot encompass Him and veils cannot cover Him — the veil between Him and His creation is His very act of creating them, due to His transcendence from what is possible in their essences, and the possibility of what is impossible for Him, and the differentiation of the Maker from the made, the Limitless from the limited, and the Lord from the governed.

The One — without the implication of a numeral; the Creator — not in the sense of movement; the All-Seeing — not by a tool; the All-Hearing — not by the separation of an organ; the Witness — not by contact; the Hidden — not by concealment; and the Manifest, the Distinct — not by the lapsing of a distance. His pre-eternity is an endpoint for the wanderings of thoughts, and His permanence is a restraint for the aspirations of intellects. His profound nature has dazzled the windows of sight, and His existence has suppressed the wanderings of imaginations.

So whoever describes God has limited Him; whoever limits Him has numbered Him; whoever numbers Him has negated His pre-eternity; whoever says 'where' has assigned Him an endpoint; whoever says 'upon what' has isolated Him; and whoever says 'in what' has contained Him.

key_terms.أَزَلُهُ: Pre-eternity, the eternal nature of God that has no beginning
key_terms.الْبَائِنُ: Distinct, separate — God is manifest yet utterly unlike creation, not distant in space but distinct in nature
key_terms.الْمَشَاعِرُ: Senses/faculties of perception — those capacities by which created beings experience the world
key_terms.الْمُمْتَنِعَةِ: Transcendent, precluded — the Essence is beyond the capacity of human description
key_terms.كُنْهُهُ: The profound true nature/depths of a thing — here, God's innermost nature which dazzles sight

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the transcendence of God in his sermon at Kufa?
ai.summary: This hadith records Imam Sadiq (AS) correcting a false attribution — certain people were claiming that statements were made by Imam Ali (AS) that he never actually spoke. The Imam then cites the authentic sermon of Imam Ali (AS) delivered at Kufa, which is a masterpiece of apophatic theology (negative theology): God's Essence, vision, and comprehension are all beyond the capacity of attributes, senses, and imagination. The sermon's concluding logical chain — whoever describes/limits/numbers God has committed a theological error — was a key formulation of the Shia theological tradition, teaching that applying spatial or numerical categories to God negates His transcendence.
